transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-15
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 53 minutes
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Sterling CISO), Tom Walsh (Sterling Head of Platform), Sara Lee (Sterling Compliance)

[00:00:00] Alyssa Chen: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, um we're excited to walk through security and privacy details today, is this still a good time for you all?
[00:00:08] Priya Patel: yes hi alyssa thanks, we have about an hour, want to make sure we cover training-on-data question early, that's the big one for legal.
[00:00:16] Marco Diaz: absolutely we'll surface that up front. quick intro, i'm marco on the SE side, i'll go deep on encryption, audit logs, retention, and the private deployment options.
[00:00:30] Tom Walsh: great, i'll be mostly focused on network/VPC and rolling this into our platform team checks.
[00:00:36] Sara Lee: and i'll be asking about retention and PHI handling specifics.

[00:01:00] Alyssa Chen: ok quick agenda — SOC 2/ISO artifacts, training/no-train commitments, prompt and content retention, PII/PHI handling, RBAC/SSO, audit logging, KMS/encryption, data residency, then recap and next steps. sound good?
[00:01:12] Priya Patel: yes, please put the no-training confirmation on the record.

[00:02:05] Marco Diaz: to start, from a platform standpoint — Redwood offers hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC or on-prem) deployments. for the data question: hosted API by default does not use customer data to train models; we have a written policy and can provide a statement. for Private deployments, customers fully control the model and data.
[00:02:30] Priya Patel: can you confirm "does not use customer data to train" covers internal model retraining and fine-tuning by Redwood? we need explicit assurance.
[00:02:40] Marco Diaz: yes so, officially — Redwood does not train or fine-tune models on customer prompt/content for our hosted inference offering. we retain telemetry/metrics for ops but not training corpuses. i'll flag that we have a legal attestation and SOC 2 controls that we can share.
[00:02:55] Priya Patel: ok, we'll need that in writing, signed if possible.

[00:03:40] Alyssa Chen: action: we'll send the SOC 2 Type II report and the no-training statement after this call.

[00:05:00] Sara Lee: about prompt retention — if we send prompts through the API, is there any default logging/storage? what's the retention window and are there options to disable storing raw prompts?
[00:05:12] Marco Diaz: good q. by default we keep short-term request logs for debugging (configurable). for hosted customers, retention defaults are 30 days for raw prompts, longer for anonymized telemetry. we offer configuration to opt-out of raw prompt retention and instead keep only metadata. for Dedicated/Private you control retention exactly.
[00:05:35] Tom Walsh: 30 days default — that's tighter than some vendors, but we need to see details. do you support automatic redaction or PII stripping at ingestion?
[00:05:46] Marco Diaz: we have two approaches: 1) client-side redaction libraries (we can share examples), 2) server-side redaction options in our platform that can strip common PHI/PII patterns, but it depends on the model/route. server-side redaction is configurable and we can exclude raw content from logs.
[00:06:10] Priya Patel: does server-side redaction run before any telemetry is stored? we need assurance that PHI never persists in unredacted form.
[00:06:20] Marco Diaz: yes if you enable the redact-before-store toggle, Redwood will apply redaction patterns immediately at ingestion before storing raw inputs. we'll include the exact flow diagram in the doc pack.

[00:07:05] Sara Lee: on PII/PHI classification — do you provide any built-in detection models or is that customer responsibility?
[00:07:12] Marco Diaz: we provide baseline detectors and regex-based rules; for high-sensitivity workflows we recommend client-side deterministic redaction + our server-side detectors as a second layer. we'll share recommended patterns used by other healthcare customers.

[00:09:00] Alyssa Chen: switching to encryption and KMS — marco?
[00:09:06] Marco Diaz: sure. all data at rest is encrypted. for hosted customers we use provider-managed keys by default, and we support customer-managed keys via KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault) for Dedicated and Private. keys can be rotated; we maintain key usage logs and can surface those in audit logs. if you need HSM-level control, Private deployment lets you integrate with on-prem HSM.
[00:09:35] Tom Walsh: is envelope encryption supported end-to-end? we need to know if any plaintext persists in our VPC or in Redwood-managed infra.
[00:09:45] Marco Diaz: envelope encryption is supported for Dedicated and Private. for hosted, Redwood decrypts in our serving layer to run inference; however raw prompts can be configured to never be stored. if you need zero-plaintext in our infra, Private/on-prem is the recommended path.

[00:10:30] Priya Patel: audit logs — we need immutable logs for all request headers, actions, admin changes, and key usage. retention policy? exportability?
[00:10:40] Marco Diaz: audit logs include request metadata, admin activity, model version changes, rollouts, and KMS key usage. logs are tamper-evident; we support export via S3/GCS sinks and syslog hooks. retention is configurable; default is 90 days for full logs but can be extended as an enterprise add-on.
[00:11:05] Sara Lee: tamper-evident how? append-only storage?
[00:11:10] Marco Diaz: we use a signing mechanism and versioned storage so any modification is detectable. we'll include the whitepaper excerpt in the artifacts.

[00:12:00] Tom Walsh: what about SSO and RBAC — we run Okta; we need SCIM and SAML, and fine-grained roles for model access, routes, and billing visibility.
[00:12:10] Alyssa Chen: we support SAML 2.0, OIDC, SCIM provisioning, and RBAC that can be mapped to your groups. roles include Admin, Developer, Auditor, Billing, and custom roles.
[00:12:25] Tom Walsh: can we restrict access so only certain users can view raw prompts or export logs?
[00:12:32] Marco Diaz: yes, audit/export permissions are separate. you can create roles that exclude raw content read permissions; you can also require an additional approval workflow for exports.

[00:13:15] Priya Patel: data residency — our policy requires patient data to remain in the EU. do you have EU regions?
[00:13:22] Marco Diaz: yes, Redwood has EU regions and supports regional routing. for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private with VPC peering in the EU. Hosted can be region-restricted as well but we need contractual SLAs for residency-only deployments.
[00:13:40] Sara Lee: ok, we may need a contract addendum.

[00:14:30] Alyssa Chen: a quick clarifying question on PHI — are customers allowed to send PHI through hosted API during a pilot?
[00:14:38] Marco Diaz: short answer: yes with controls, but you must enable redact-before-store, sign the DPA, and ideally use customer-managed keys and region restrictions. for long-term production we recommend Dedicated or Private for maximum isolation.
[00:15:00] Priya Patel: our legal team will push back on hosted unless there's a hard no-train guarantee and strong controls.
[00:15:08] Alyssa Chen: understood. we'll provide the attestation plus the SOC 2 artifacts.

[00:16:30] Tom Walsh: about model versions and rollouts — if Redwood performs a model update, can we pin to a model snapshot so behavior won't change mid-flight?
[00:16:38] Marco Diaz: yes. pinning to model versions is supported; you can request pinned rollouts for the pilot. automatic fallbacks are configurable as well.

[00:18:00] Sara Lee: logging and analytics — does Redwood keep token-level logs with request/response text? we need to avoid storing responses that may echo PHI.
[00:18:12] Marco Diaz: token-level debug logs are available but disabled by default; we recommend keeping only aggregate usage for billing and enabling token-level logs only during troubleshooting windows, with automatic purge.

[00:19:20] Priya Patel: incident response and breach notifications — typical SLAs?
[00:19:26] Alyssa Chen: Redwood provides incident playbook in the SOC pack. for critical incidents we have 24/7 on-call and notify customers within contractual timelines (e.g., 72 hours depending on severity and regulation). we'll include the incident response runbook.

[00:21:00] Tom Walsh: integrations — can we ingest events to our SIEM?
[00:21:06] Marco Diaz: yes, we support SIEM export via syslog and webhooks and can set up a dedicated integration for you.

[00:22:00] Sara Lee: curious about retention deletion — if we request deletion of historical logs containing PHI, is that immediate? how do we prove deletion?
[00:22:10] Marco Diaz: deletion requests are processed and we can provide a deletion certificate for the requested artifacts. we also support automated deletion policies and legal hold exceptions if needed.

[00:24:00] Priya Patel: can you walk through the hosted telemetry flow quickly — what gets sent to Redwood and what stays client-side?
[00:24:10] Marco Diaz: sure — at a high level: request metadata (timestamp, model id, route, client id) is always sent. raw prompt and response are optional and depend on your retention settings. telemetry like latencies and error rates are stored as aggregates. with redact-before-store enabled, we apply regex or ML detectors to mask PHI before any persistence.

[00:26:30] Alyssa Chen: quick note from legal perspective — we'll attach the DPA and data processing terms to the art pack.
[00:26:40] Priya Patel: ok thanks, we want a clause that prevents Redwood from using any customer content to improve models — not just in practice but contractually.
[00:26:50] Alyssa Chen: we can add explicit contractual language, yes.

[00:28:00] Marco Diaz: small nuance: some telemetry e.g., error traces may contain fragments; we have a policy to scrub and not use them for training. the SOC 2 control and DPA will reflect that.
[00:28:18] Priya Patel: we'll want to see examples of scrubbed vs unsrubbed logs.

[00:30:00] Tom Walsh: performance and metrics — if we opt for Dedicated, what's the isolation (GPU pools) and how do you guarantee latency?
[00:30:10] Marco Diaz: Dedicated provides reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and SLA-backed latency targets. we'll include the Dedicated SLA and typical perf numbers for the model families you're interested in.

[00:32:00] Sara Lee: onboarding & audits — do you support third-party audits or on-site security reviews?
[00:32:07] Alyssa Chen: we support security questionnaires, and for enterprise customers we can coordinate audits and provide artifact packs. on-site reviews are possible for Dedicated/Private with an NDA.

[00:34:00] Priya Patel: around compliance — do you have attestations for HIPAA specifically?
[00:34:07] Marco Diaz: we don't issue a HIPAA-specific certification but we have controls, BAAs (Business Associate Agreements) and healthcare customers use our Dedicated/Private patterns plus the DPA and BAA. we'll share the BAA template.

[00:36:00] Alyssa Chen: ok time check — about 15 minutes left, want to go through a quick recap?
[00:36:08] Priya Patel: yes please.

[00:36:15] Alyssa Chen: recap: 1) Redwood confirms no-training-on-customer-data for hosted inference and will provide written attestation. 2) Prompt retention: default 30 days for raw prompts but configurable and opt-out available; server-side redact-before-store toggle exists. 3) PII/PHI: client-side redaction recommended + server-side detectors; Dedicated/Private recommended for production PHI workloads. 4) Encryption: provider-managed keys by default, customer-managed KMS supported, envelope encryption and HSM available for Private. 5) Audit logs: tamper-evident, exportable, default 90-day retention, extendable. 6) RBAC/SSO: SAML/SCIM/OIDC supported; fine-grained roles and export permissions. 7) Data residency: EU regions and Dedicated/Private for strict requirements. 8) Next steps: share SOC2, KMS guide, sample prompts, schedule pilot kickoff.
[00:37:05] Priya Patel: that matches our notes. we'll want the SOC2 and the no-train attestation early.
[00:37:12] Alyssa Chen: action items noted.

[00:40:00] Tom Walsh: one last question on evidence — for deletion certificates, do you include hashes or unique IDs we can verify?
[00:40:08] Marco Diaz: yes we can supply deletion certificates referencing object IDs and timestamps; we'll include the format in the artifacts.

[00:42:00] Sara Lee: question — are there any scenarios where Redwood could inadvertently use customer content? accidental logs used for debugging?
[00:42:10] Marco Diaz: accidental captures are possible but we have controls: masking, manual review only with approvals, and scrubbed copies are used; in the case of an accidental capture the incident process triggers immediate deletion and you get notification.

[00:44:00] Priya Patel: ok thanks, that's helpful. next steps again — SOC2, DPA/BAA, KMS guide, redact patterns, sample pilot plan and schedule.
[00:44:12] Alyssa Chen: we'll send those items. anything else?
[00:44:20] Tom Walsh: we'll prepare sample prompts and a short list of PHI scenarios for the pilot.
[00:44:26] Sara Lee: i'll prep compliance checklist and any regulatory constraints to share.

[00:46:00] Alyssa Chen: great, we'll follow up and propose a pilot kickoff date. thanks everyone for your time.
[00:46:10] Priya Patel: thanks all.
[00:46:15] Marco Diaz: thanks.

[00:52:55] System: Recording stopped.

Notes: transcript contains minor transcription artifacts — names and acronyms occasionally mis-transcribed. References
- Artifacts to be shared: SOC 2 Type II report, ISO artifacts excerpt, DPA and BAA template, KMS/encryption integration guide, redact-before-store flow diagram, Dedicated SLA, deletion certificate format, sample redaction rules.
